question: Which feature of the Indian Constitution reflects the idea that the powers of government are divided among the executive, legislative, and judicial branches to prevent the concentration of power?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Separation of powers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• ** Executive**

 
 
• Article 53 of the Constitution of India states that the executive power of the Union shall be vested in the President. 
 
• However, the President exercises this power on the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister. 
 
• This is known as the "advice and consent" system.
 
• The President has the power to appoint the Prime Minister, dissolve the Lok Sabha, and make certain key appointments. 
 
• However, he can only do these things on the advice of the Council of Ministers. 
 
• The President is also the Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces.
 
• In practice, the real executive power in India lies with the Council of Ministers. 
 
• The Prime Minister is the head of the Council of Ministers and is responsible for the day-to-day running of the government. 
 
• The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.
 
• The Parliament is the supreme law-making body in India. 
 
• It has the power to make laws, amend the Constitution, and remove the President from office. 
 
• However, the Parliament cannot interfere with the executive powers of the President.
 
• So, while the executive power of the Union vests in the President, it is actually exercised by the Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister. 
 
• This is a reflection of the parliamentary system of government that is practised in India.
 
 
 
• **​ Legislative**
 
 
• The legislature is prohibited from acting in an executive or judicial capacity by the doctrine of separation of powers.
 
• Legislative and judicial authority are not subject to executive control.
 
• and the judicial branch is not permitted to use the other two powers.
 
• As with the British Parliament, the Indian Parliament is therefore able to pass legislation that both quantitatively and qualitatively delegated legislative power.
 
• In the absence of any constitutional restrictions, any amount of legislative power could be delegated as long as the delegating body maintained its own legislative authority.
 
 
 
• **Judicial **
 
 
• The power of judicial review relates to the Review of the organization of the judiciary.
 
• It is the power exerted by the courts of a country to examine the actions of the legislatures, and executive and administrative arms of government and to ensure that such actions conform to the provisions of the nation’s Constitution.
 
• The judicial review implies the power to ensure that laws passed by the legislature are in compliance with the provisions of the Constitution.
 
• Judicial review is considered a basic structure of the constitution (Indira Gandhi vs Raj Narain Case 1975).
